analysis.investment_thesis: Cemindia (formerly ITD Cementation) is a direct play on India's infrastructure decade — ports, maritime, MRT, airports, tunnels — and the numbers in FY23–25 are exceptional: revenue nearly tripling to INR 9,097 Cr with ROCE at 27.6% and ROE at 21.8%. However, a change of promoter to UAE-based Renew Exim DMCC in August 2025 introduces governance uncertainty that prevents me from going beyond a HOLD at this stage.
key_strengths: Exceptional ROCE of 27.6% and ROE of 21.8% — rare quality for a construction company; shows disciplined capital deployment in niche, high-value segments like maritime and underground
Revenue accelerated from INR 2,728 Cr (FY21) to INR 9,097 Cr (FY25) — a 35% CAGR over 4 years — directly capturing the National Infrastructure Pipeline tailwind
D/E of 0.48x is comfortable for a project contractor; promoter holding at 67.46% shows majority ownership commitment
key_risks: New promoter (Renew Exim DMCC, UAE) took over in August 2025 from the established Italian Thai group — a completely new controlling shareholder means unknown execution culture, strategic priorities, and risk appetite
OCF fell sharply from INR 704 Cr (FY24) to INR 203 Cr (FY25) despite much higher revenue — working capital strain and project-cycle timing risk are inherent in large civil contracts
Construction is an order-book business; any slowdown in government infrastructure spending or execution delays can compress margins rapidly from the current 7.7% operating margin
red_flags: Promoter identity change is the single biggest flag — I need at least 2–3 years of track record under Renew Exim DMCC before adding conviction; integrity of new promoter unproven in Indian markets
P/B of 5.44x is elevated for a construction company — leaves limited margin of safety if order book slips
Finance costs rising (INR 165 Cr to INR 229 Cr in 2 years) alongside total debt growing to INR 961 Cr — leverage is creeping up as the company scales
analysis.detailed_analysis: The underlying operating business is genuinely impressive — Cemindia's specialisation in complex maritime, tunnel, and MRT work gives it a defensible niche in India's infrastructure boom, and ROCE of 27.6% shows that the company earns well above its cost of capital. Net profit compounding from INR 16 Cr (FY21) to INR 373 Cr (FY25) is a textbook turnaround. Forward P/E of 17x is not demanding given these returns. However, the August 2025 promoter change is a material governance event I cannot overlook. In India, promoter quality and continuity are paramount, and I have seen too many good businesses derailed by new owners with different priorities. I would watch two or three quarters of results under the new promoter, check related-party disclosures carefully, and wait for a pullback before building a position — the story is right but the governance piece needs time to validate.
